sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Demographic Changes & Migration** covers population growth, density, distribution, literacy, sex ratio, and spatial movement of people.
**Census 2011** is the baseline official data source for UPSSSC PET, as subsequent censuses were delayed.
Geographical focus spans across **India** at national scale and specifically **Uttar Pradesh** state demographics.
Data is compiled and published by the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner** under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Crucial for socio-economic planning, resource allocation, and frequently tested via **Census 2011** direct questions in UPSSSC PET.
**Population Growth Rate**, **Population Density**, **Literacy Rate**, **Sex Ratio**, **Urbanization**, and **Push-Pull Migration Factors**.
Direct factual questions on state/national rankings, literacy figures, and density indices carry guaranteed marks.
India's population was **121.08 crore** in 2011; UP is the **most populous state** with ~19.98 crore people.

items.title: 1. Population Growth & Census Fundamentals
items.content:
• Census in India is conducted decennially under the **Census Act 1948**.
• First complete census took place in **1881** under **Lord Ripon**.
• Year **1921** is known as the **Year of Great Divide** due to negative population growth (-0.31%).
• Year **1951** is termed the **Year of Population Explosion** due to sudden post-independence mortality decline.
• **Mnemonic for Census Decades:** **'RIP-1881'** (Ripon initiated Population in 1881).

items.title: 2. Population Density and Distribution
items.content:
• **Population Density** is measured as persons per square kilometer.
• India's overall population density in 2011 was **382 persons/sq km**.
• **Bihar** has the highest population density (**1106 persons/sq km**).
• **Arunachal Pradesh** has the lowest population density (**17 persons/sq km**).
• **Uttar Pradesh** population density is **829 persons/sq km**.
• **Mnemonic for Density Extremes:** **'BAP'** (Bihar Above Peak density, Arunachal lowest Population).

items.title: 3. Literacy Rate Dynamics
items.content:
• Total literacy rate of India in 2011 reached **74.04%** (Male: **82.14%**, Female: **65.46%**).
• **Kerala** ranks first in overall literacy (**94.00%**).
• **Bihar** ranks lowest in overall literacy (**61.80%**).
• **Uttar Pradesh** literacy rate is **67.7%** (Male: **77.3%**, Female: **57.2%**).
• **Mnemonic for Literacy Leaders:** **'KB-MF'** (Kerala Best, Bihar Floor; Male First).

items.title: 4. Sex Ratio Variations
items.content:
• **Sex Ratio** is defined as the number of females per 1000 males.
• India's overall sex ratio in 2011 was **943 females per 1000 males**.
• **Kerala** recorded the highest sex ratio (**1084**).
• **Haryana** recorded the lowest sex ratio (**879**).
• **Uttar Pradesh** sex ratio stands at **912**.
• Child sex ratio (0-6 age group) for India is **919** (lowest in **Haryana** at **834**).

items.title: 5. Migration Patterns & Theories
items.content:
• **Migration** involves the permanent or semi-permanent change of residence across administrative boundaries.
• **Push Factors:** Unemployment, poverty, natural disasters, lack of healthcare (drives people *out*).
• **Pull Factors:** Better job opportunities, higher education, better living standards (attracts people *in*).
• **Stream of Migration:** Rural to Urban is the largest internal migration stream in India, driven predominantly by employment.

items.title: 6. Urbanization Trends
items.content:
• India's urban population percentage in 2011 was **31.16%**.
• **Goa** is the most urbanized state (**62.17%** urban population).
• **Himachal Pradesh** is the least urbanized state (**10.03%** urban population).
• **Uttar Pradesh** urban population percentage is **22.27%**.
• Mega-cities like **Mumbai**, **Delhi**, and **Kolkata** act as major urban magnets.

items.definition: Remember **'1-3-4'** for UP: **1st** in total population, **3rd** in geographical area, **4th** in population density among major states.
Use acronym **'U-M-B'** (Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar) - Uttar Pradesh is #1, Maharashtra #2, Bihar #3.
Use acronym **'S-M-A'** (Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh) - Sikkim has the lowest population in India.
Remember **'K-B'** poles: **Kerala** is top in literacy, **Bihar** is bottom in literacy.
Remember **'B-A'** poles: **Bihar** is top in density (1106), **Arunachal** is bottom in density (17).
India's growth rate was **17.7%**; rhyme it as **'Seventeen point seven, growing under heaven'** for quick recall.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Total Population with Density
items.definition: Students confuse Uttar Pradesh being #1 in population with density. UP is **#1 in population** but ranks **4th in population density** among major states (Bihar is #1 in density).

items.term: Mistake 2: Confusing Overall Sex Ratio with Child Sex Ratio
items.definition: India's overall sex ratio is **943**, but the 0-6 age group Child Sex Ratio is **919**. Do not mix up these two distinct Census 2011 metrics.

items.term: Mistake 3: Year of Great Divide vs Population Explosion
items.definition: **1921** is the **Year of Great Divide** (population dropped slightly). **1951** is the **Year of Population Explosion** (growth rate spiked sharply post-independence).
Census calculates literacy rate for population aged **7 years and above**, not for newborn infants. Students often forget the age cutoff.

items.term: Mistake 5: Urbanization Percentage vs Absolute Urban Numbers
items.definition: **Goa** has the highest *percentage* of urbanization (**62.17%**), but **Maharashtra** has the highest *absolute* number of urban dwellers.

items.term: Mistake 6: Rural vs Urban Share in UP
items.definition: UP is predominantly rural with **77.73%** rural population, while only **22.7%** live in urban areas. Do not overestimate UP's urbanization.
All official UPSSSC PET demographic questions are based on the **2011 Census**, India's 15th decennial census.
India's population crossed **1.21 billion** in 2011, accounting for **17.5%** of the global population.
UP houses **19.98 crore** people (**16.5%** of India), making it more populous than many sovereign countries.
India's growth rate slowed to **17.7%** during 2001-2011, compared to **21.54%** in the previous decade.
National average density reached **382 persons/sq km**, with **Bihar** recording the highest density (**1106**).
India's sex ratio improved to **943**, led by **Kerala** (**1084**), while Haryana lagged at **879**.
National literacy reached **74.04%**, with male literacy at **82.14%** and female literacy at **65.46%**.
UP's literacy rate is **67.7%**, featuring a wide gender gap (Male: **77.3%**, Female: **57.2%**).
India's urban population stands at **31.16%**, reflecting a steady rural-to-urban demographic transition.
Internal migration is dominated by **rural-to-urban** streams, driven primarily by economic and employment opportunities.

upscNotes.content: Memorize exact figures for India and UP total population, literacy rates, and sex ratios as UPSSSC PET frequently asks direct numerical matching questions.
Focus heavily on extreme states (highest and lowest) in density, literacy, sex ratio, and urbanization for both India and Uttar Pradesh.
Do not assume UP ranks first in population density just because it ranks first in total population; Bihar holds the top density rank.
Watch out for questions specifying the 'Child Sex Ratio' (0-6 years) versus the 'Overall Sex Ratio' as examiners frequently swap these numbers in options.

keyTakeaways: Census 2011 is the statutory baseline for all UPSSSC PET demographic questions.
Uttar Pradesh represents 16.5% of India's total population with 19.98 crore inhabitants.
India's overall literacy rate is 74.04%, with Kerala leading and Bihar trailing.
Population density is highest in Bihar (1106) and lowest in Arunachal Pradesh (17).
Rural-to-urban migration remains the primary driver of internal spatial demographic shifts in India.
